name: Trigger.dev
description: Durable background job and workflow orchestration for production AI agents and event-driven apps. Provides step-by-step execution with retry logic, real-time observability, and webhook-triggered workflows. The default orchestration layer in production agent stacks.

ecosystem_fit.notes: Used in the solana-trading-agent workflow for durable agent execution with Helius webhook triggers.
Used in base-onchain-ai-agent for durable step execution.
Farcaster social AI agents use Trigger.dev for durable response generation triggered by Neynar webhooks.
General background job and orchestration use across Ethereum agent patterns.

common_pairings.context: Helius webhooks trigger Trigger.dev jobs. The event-driven architecture for Solana agent workflows — Helius detects the onchain event, Trigger.dev executes the agent response durably.
Trigger.dev orchestrates the outer workflow (retries, step logging); Vercel AI SDK handles the LLM reasoning within each step.
Neynar webhooks fire Trigger.dev jobs when Farcaster events occur. Trigger.dev provides the durable execution wrapper around agent social actions.
Alchemy webhooks trigger Trigger.dev jobs for EVM event-driven workflows on Base and Ethereum.

trust_evidence.description: Trigger.dev is cited as the default orchestration layer in every production AI agent workflow in WORKFLOWS.md. Appears in solana-trading-agent, base-onchain-ai-agent, and farcaster-social-ai-agent.
Trigger.dev v3 maintains active documentation for background jobs, durable execution, and webhook-triggered workflows.
Active development with v3 representing a significant architectural improvement over v2. Used in production by teams building AI-native applications.

scale_guidance.hackathon: Skip orchestration at hackathon scale. Use Trigger.dev from MVP onward.
scale_guidance.mvp: Add Trigger.dev early — debugging autonomous agents without execution traces is extremely difficult. The visibility it provides pays for itself immediately.
scale_guidance.production: Required for production agents. Production trading agents without durable orchestration will have unexplainable failures. Configure concurrency limits to prevent runaway agent executions.

alternatives.when_to_prefer: When simpler event-driven workflows are needed with less complex retry requirements. Inngest has a gentler learning curve and strong Next.js integration.
When very complex multi-step workflows require strong durable execution guarantees with fine-grained state management. Higher operational complexity than Trigger.dev.

anti_patterns: Using Trigger.dev v2 patterns with v3 — breaking changes in the SDK between versions. Check v3 migration guide.
Skipping orchestration for production agents — autonomous agents without execution tracing will have failures that are impossible to debug.
Not implementing concurrency limits — unconstrained agent workflows can exhaust LLM API quotas at machine speed.
